claims.text: Equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi is a high-entropy alloy.
Equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi has a random solid-solution structure.
Introducing a small, controlled amount of interstitial nitrogen into equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi will enhance its magnetocaloric properties relative to the undoped alloy.
Nitrogen can be incorporated interstitially into CoCrFeMnNi at controlled concentrations.
Interstitial nitrogen will modify the lattice parameters of CoCrFeMnNi.
Interstitial nitrogen will modify local atomic environments in CoCrFeMnNi.
Nitrogen addition is expected to cause subtle lattice expansion.
Nitrogen addition is expected to produce local electronic variations.
Nitrogen-induced lattice and electronic changes will alter magnetic exchange interactions.
Altered magnetic exchange interactions may broaden or sharpen the magnetic phase transition.
Changes to the magnetic phase transition will increase the magnetic entropy change.
Magnetic entropy change is a key metric of the magnetocaloric effect.
Nitrogen-doped CoCrFeMnNi will exhibit a larger and more tunable magnetocaloric effect around its Curie temperature than undoped CoCrFeMnNi.
The improved magnetocaloric effect may appear as a higher magnetic entropy change and/or a higher adiabatic temperature change.
Any enhancement will be sensitive to nitrogen concentration and microstructural homogeneity.
Excessive nitrogen doping or phase separation may negate the proposed tuning of magnetic interactions.
The literature supports a role for interstitial atoms in modifying the physical properties of high-entropy alloys.
The specific effect of nitrogen on the magnetocaloric behavior of CoCrFeMnNi remains quantitatively unestablished.
